top.title: A C.J. Stroud flu game? Sick and with the chills, Texans QB throws for 5 TDs to beat Chargers
top.description: Back in his native Southern California, C.J. Stroud turned in one of the best games of his career as the Texans stayed in the playoff hunt with a win over the Chargers. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) INGLEWOOD, Calif. - When C.J. Stroud woke up in his hotel bed Sunday morning in downtown Los Angeles, he was still feeling under the weather. All week he had been dealing with some kind of illness that he said gave him chills and "all the things." He said he barely practiced Thursday. Whatever he had, it was still with him. Yet, some six hours later, he went on to have one of the best games of his career. Stroud, who was playing in front of friends and family near his hometown of Rancho Cucamonga , threw for a season-high 384 yards, a career-high five touchdowns and just one interception in Houston's 44-22 rout of the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) on Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The 44 points scored were a season high for the Texans' offense, which has often delivered time and time again, especially on the road. The Texans improved to 3-5 on the season. It was the type of performance that will put Stroud in the MVP conversation if he can continue playing this way. It is the type of performance that will have some suggesting that the Texans can make a run towards the playoffs. "He really gives that confidence to the entire team," coach DeMeco Ryans said of Stroud. "When the defensive guys, they see him up making plays, everyone is excited. Everyone knows the type of energy, the type of momentum that that brings to our entire team when he's making those plays and he's done it all year." The Texans are currently 1 ½ games behind the Patriots for that final wild-card spot with nine games remaining. They face the Browns, who are also 1 ½ games ahead of them, next Sunday in Cleveland. But based on their upcoming schedule, and how Stroud is playing, anything is possible, especially if the defense can gain some momentum too. Though the performance from the defense wasn't perfect, Sunday's game against the NFL's worst offense was a step in the right direction. The Texans tied a franchise record with eight sacks on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. They also forced two turnovers - an interception by cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. and a fumble. But the offense, which had 485 yards of total offense, was the story of this game. And it started with Stroud, who became just the fourth quarterback younger than 26 years old with at least 350 passing yards and five touchdown passes in multiple games, joining Patrick Mahomes, Dan Marino and Matthew Stafford. The other game Stroud achieved that stat line was during his 2023 rookie season, when he threw five touchdowns in a thrilling 39-37 win over the Bucs . top.description: Texas Longhorns defensive back Graceson Littleton (29) and Texas Longhorns linebacker Justin Cryer (28) defend Missouri Tigers wide receiver Cayden Lee (19) during the game against Missouri at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium in Columbia on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. The road trips are too grueling. And the Longhorns, with their abundance of resources and Big 12 background, are just too soft. But as the team proved yet again in Saturday's 34-20 win at No. 18 Missouri, No. 7 Texas (7-2, 4-2 SEC) has the steel needed for a run at the College Football Playoff. The Longhorns improved to 7-2 in true SEC road games since joining the conference in 2024, a rate of success that must impress even the most ardent burnt-orange skeptic. "Our guys, they're not naive to noise," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said after Saturday's win. "As much as I would love to say, ‘Hey, tune it all out,' I could hear the talk getting on the plane (Friday). I could hear the talk when we got here. Nobody thought we were going to come here and win the game. Nobody thought we were tough enough at the line of scrimmage. Everyone thought we'd get pushed around." top.title: ‘We call him…’: Bones Hyland says T-Wolves have a new nickname for Joan Beringer after his 'broken nose'
top.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves made it four wins in a row after beating the Utah Jazz 115-100. LaMelo Ball stole the show as he always does, while Ayo Dosunmu scored 26 points. But the bench more than played its part, especially Bones Hyland and Joan Beringer. The former has a nickname for the Frenchman now. Bones Hyland says Joan Beringer is called ‘The Batman’ and shares a ‘funny story’ Beringer suffered a nasal fracture during the Minnesota Timberwolves’ win over the New Orleans Pelicans in the NBA Cup. The Frenchman suffered an inadvertent elbow to his face. He still scored two free throws with blood coming out of his nose, but he didn’t return after being diagnosed with a fracture. There were fears that Beringer would be sidelined, but the teenager played against the Jazz on Sunday night while wearing a protective mask. Hyland claimed that Beringer even wore the mask in the locker room when he first got it, thus leading to a new nickname. He said: “We call him ‘The Batman’. It’s a funny story. We were in the locker room, and he had that mask on. They told him he had to wear it. He ain’t take it off in the locker room. “I was like: ‘Joan, you ain’t even on the court right now. You can take your mask off’. But that was the first time he was wearing the mask with a broken nose. “But he’s a warrior, bro. We love Joan. He has come in with young legs and runs the floor for us, blocks shots, and makes shots go left or right. We love Joan!” ‘The Batman’ is a really cool nickname for Beringer, but what’s better is his performances for the Minnesota Timberwolves this season. The teenager has impressed everyone and has earned a lot of praise, including one from his country’s biggest basketball star, Victor Wembanyama. Beringer is not a starter yet, but if he keeps developing at the same rate, he will become a star in the not-too-distant future. top.title: Nick Wright calls Patrick Mahomes a ‘cyborg’ after getting injured with hit during Chiefs win over Jets
top.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes pushed through a serious hit in their 35-12 win over the New York Jets. Mahomes did not miss a single offensive snap in the win, going 23/31 on pass attempts for 242 yards, two TDs, and a 117.9 passer rating. He also rushed for eight yards on two carries in a strong performance. Mahomes was tackled by Jets EDGE David Bailey in the second quarter and appeared to suffer an elbow injury, but his resolute toughness made him push through the discomfort and finish the win after avoiding major injury. Patrick Mahomes hailed as a cyborg by Nick Wright Watching Mahomes take that rough hit and escape without injury left FOX Sports’ Nick Wright in awe of the 33-year-old QB. “Also… Never a doubt. Mahomes is a cyborg. 99% of QBs have their elbow dislocated on that hit. He missed zero snaps. They’ll be 8-2 heading into Buffalo.” It’s since been confirmed that Mahomes’ injury is an elbow strain/sprain after post-game MRIs, with the QB likely not missing their game against the Atlanta Falcons on November 15. Mahomes admitted after the win that the hit from Bailey had a major impact on his performance, as he struggled to throw the ball as deep and precisely as he normally can. Nonetheless, even a slightly wounded Mahomes would be a better option than backup QB Justin Fields for the Chiefs right now, especially as they look to challenge the 7-2 Denver Broncos for THE top spot in the AFC West. While Mahomes has not been among the MVP contenders this season, he has had a strong comeback season after rushing through recovery from a torn ACL. Over the season, Mahomes has thrown 177/263 for 2,037 yards, 14 TDs, and four INTs for a 101.8 passer rating. Avoiding a season-ending elbow injury on that play was a moment of good fortune for the Chiefs, and the franchise will hope that fortune pushes them through till the end of the season. top.title: AI echo chambers and sanity in tech leadership: Three case studies
top.description: "AI delusion" remains loosely defined, but most of us know it when we see it: exaggerated faith in the technology's power, applicability, or nature, coupled with a refusal to acknowledge its limitations. It's bad in the individual, as when an elderly relative emails you a hallucination-laden ChatGPT summary. It's worse in management, when your boss insists that AI slop is genius marketing content at a bargain rate. It is terrifying in tech CEOs. It is not, thankfully, compulsory. Consider three recent examples of technology leadership in the age of AI. One would be Pythonesque were the disconnect with engineers and the public not so profound. Another risks becoming a business-school case study in how to demolish customer trust. The third offers something less fashionable: robust pragmatism. Saving the best till last, y'all. Case 1: we present for your consideration Sam Altman of OpenAI, one of the few actually at the controls of the singularity machine. It seems churlish to pluck just one luscious fruit out of that cornucopia of choices, yet we must. Sam Altman thinks it is a sin against the natural order that so much RAM is idling in machines owned by individuals, organizations, and anywhere that isn't Big AI . It's oh so inefficient. How convenient that the efficient allocation of scarce resources should favor the business he runs. Free market schmarket. Altman has since said his remarks were taken out of context and that he wants consumers to have as much memory as they like. The efficiency argument still reveals whose priorities come first. This is the best kind of delusion, one with an undeniable truth at its core – memory does indeed get used far more intensively in AI model makers and inference servers than in your laptop. For a business selling the future, treating privately owned hardware as an inefficient allocation of resources has a distinctly Soviet flavor, and the American right has vowed to stamp out socialist extremism. Get on with it, chaps, you've only got two years left . That Altman can't see this is the best bit of the misconception. There are two potential root causes of this Marxist-Leninist-Altmanism. One is that he's mathed the math and worked out that the only way OpenAI can hit the numbers is if it gets every last byte in the world, hot off the fab. The other is that you can't run on-prem on an 8 GB state-mandated Chromebook, and on-prem is otherwise going to twist his melon until it falls off. Case 2: Andy Yen, CEO of Proton, the company behind Proton Mail and Proton VPN. You, me, and the household cat know ProtonMail as the secondary email that's worth paying for. You want the best recovery backup email for Gmail, you want it as an accessible end-to-end encrypted email service. top.title: DisCos Apologise To Nigerians Over Power Outages
top.description: Electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) have apologised to Nigerians over persistent electricity shortages across the country, acknowledging the hardship caused by weeks of prolonged blackouts. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan, tendered the apology on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . “I’d like to first of all start by apologising to Nigerians. Apology is needed; it is essential because Nigerians have been taken through this problem over the past few weeks,” he said. Oduntan also criticised what he described as a return to the blame game among operators in the electricity sector, recalling that similar disagreements between stakeholders had characterised the industry between 2016 and 2019. He said distribution companies, transmission operators, generation companies and gas suppliers had previously blamed one another for poor electricity supply instead of addressing the underlying problems. “Our major problem is that we have started that very wrong route that we went through between 2016 and 2019. What is that? Blame game. “Part of what happened at that time is that people will blame the DisCos, DisCos will blame TCN, TCN will blame GenCos, GenCos will blame the gas suppliers, and gas suppliers will blame payment issues. We have returned to that, and I think there is a need to arrest that,” he said. Oduntan Questions Conflicting Explanations A combo of the Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan and electricity installations. The ANED spokesperson also expressed concern over statements issued by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) regarding the factors responsible for the electricity shortages. He said NISO had attributed the supply challenges partly to low water levels and inadequate gas supply, while the NNPC subsequently issued a statement indicating that gas was available. Oduntan, however, questioned the information provided by the national oil company, insisting that it should clarify whether outstanding payments were affecting gas supply to power generation companies. “From the NNPC statement, it is very clear that they came to tell us half-truths. What I would have expected NNPC to do is to go ahead and talk to us whether there are payment issues. We need to know whether gas was paid for and delivered, who did, who didn’t,” he said. The ANED CEO urged the Minister of Power to intervene by bringing the relevant stakeholders together to establish the actual causes of the shortages. “This back and forth blame game between gas suppliers, NNPC and, of course, TCN or NISO, I think the Minister of Power needs to take charge. nigeria.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation IGBO DANU II, under the 2 Division of the Nigerian Army, have neutralised a suspected criminal and recovered an AK-47 rifle and other weapons during an operation in the Old Oyo National Park. The operation, conducted in collaboration with hybrid forces, also led to the destruction of temporary shelters suspected to have been used as hideouts by criminal elements operating in the forest. The Nigerian Army disclosed this in a statement, saying the encounter occurred on November 7, 2026, when troops conducting operations within the park engaged suspected criminals who fled upon sighting the advancing forces. The statement said the troops subsequently recovered an AK-47 rifle, one empty magazine and a Dane gun from the area. It added that during a follow-up operation on November 8, troops discovered the corpse of one of the fleeing suspects, confirming that one criminal element had been neutralised. According to the Army, the destruction of the temporary shelters was aimed at disrupting criminal activities and denying the suspects safe havens within the forested area. It said troops, in collaboration with other security stakeholders, remained committed to sustaining operations to dismantle criminal networks, deny them operational bases and restore security across the 2 Division Area of Responsibility. The Army added that exploitation of the general area was ongoing to track fleeing suspects and prevent them from regrouping. nigeria.title: Against All Odds: HomeWork Group, Africa Hands Over 14 Luxury Maisonettes at King’s Court, Ikeja GRA
nigeria.description: GMD reaffirms commitment as firm records second project completion in 2026 HomeWork Group Africa has handed over 14 fully serviced three- and four-bedroom maisonettes at King’s Court, a residential development located on Adekunle Fajuyi Street, Ikeja GRA, Lagos. The handover ceremony, held on October 27, 2026, marked the completion of the project, which commenced in July 2021. King’s Court features spacious living areas and kitchens, private courtyards designed to promote cross-ventilation, large windows that allow natural lighting and deep balconies. The estate also provides power, water, security, CCTV, parking, a gym and a swimming pool. One of the homeowners commended the quality of the completed development and the consistent communication maintained by the company throughout the project. Speaking at the handover, the Group Managing Director of HomeWork Group Africa expressed gratitude for the completion and reaffirmed the company’s commitment to delivering quality homes. “ God establishes the works of our hands, and now we have the thrill of yet another completion. For us at HomeWork Group Africa, King’s Court is a story of determination. We promised our clients quality homes, and despite all odds, we have delivered.” King’s Court is the company’s second completed project in 2026, following the opening of Malvin Mall, a six-storey commercial development on Admiralty Way, Lekki, Lagos. HomeWork Group Africa is also preparing to hand over two residential developments before the end of the year. Yellowstone, located in Lekki Phase 1, comprises four terrace units and a penthouse, while Hines Court 2, situated on Freedom Way, Lekki, consists of 32 two- and three-bedroom flats. Founded in 2008, HomeWork Group Africa said it has completed more than 20 estate projects and delivered nearly 400 units. The company said the King’s Court handover further strengthens its portfolio of residential and commercial developments across Lagos. nigeria.title: 2027: I’ve laid the foundation, my second term will be consolidation – Otti
nigeria.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe, Umuahia Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Chioma Otti, has said that the achievements recorded by his administration in the last three years represent only the foundation of his development agenda, assuring that the next four and a half years will focus on consolidating the gains and entrenching reforms across the state. Otti, who stated this during the South-East Conference of Dominion City Global, held in Aba, assured residents that his administration is committed to taking the state to the next level of development. Describing the achievements of his administration as a dress rehearsal, Otti said his government is determined to deepen ongoing reforms and deliver practical development outcomes that would have a lasting impact on the lives of the people. He said, “What has happened here is what I call a dress rehearsal, to let people know that they haven’t seen anything yet. What we have built in the last three years is just the foundation. “So, the next four and a half years, we will use them to consolidate. And when I say consolidation, I mean consolidation – changes that are irreversible. “My administration is not interested in making unrealistic promises but in implementing practical policies and projects capable of transforming the state.” He disclosed that his government is working towards ensuring a constant electricity supply across the state. According to him, the move would enable Abia to strengthen its electricity regulatory framework, support power generation and distribution capacity, and facilitate the distribution of excess electricity to other parts of the state. The governor also noted that his administration had instituted a monthly media chat to ensure that residents are adequately informed about government activities, policies and achievements. Otti reiterated his administration’s commitment to fairness, equity and merit in governance, declaring that there is no state-of-origin discrimination in Abia, as everyone living in the state is regarded as an Abian and treated equally. He charged Christians to demonstrate their faith through practical actions, adding that meaningful progress requires commitment, hard work and personal responsibility, as people should not expect miracles without making the necessary efforts. The governor congratulated the leadership of Dominion City Global on the conference and the construction of its massive facility in Aba, expressing admiration for the scale of the project and commending the church for its commitment to advancing the work of God. Earlier, the president of Dominion City Church, Pastor David Ogbueli, commended the governor for demonstrating servant leadership and transforming the state through purposeful governance. nigeria.title: Olympic Judo Champion Riner Joins Fight For French Presidency
nigeria.description: France’s five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in the country’s high-stakes presidential election next year. “My name is Teddy Riner and today, I am telling you face to face: I am a candidate in the 2027 presidential election,” the 37-year-old said in a surprise announcement on social media. Riner, among France’s best-known sports figures, enters the race with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen leading in the polls to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron next year. France’s Teddy Riner (Blue) reacts after beating South Korea’s Kim Min-jong in the judo men’s +100kg gold bout of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games at the Champ-de-Mars Arena, in Paris on August 2, 2024. He has publicly said he was very worried about the “rise of the far right” in France. Riner has won five Olympic gold medals in judo. He won the heavyweight division at the 2012, 2016 and 2024 Olympics and mixed team golds at the 2020 and 2024 Games. Riner has also won 11 world titles. Another French star judoka, David Douillet, was elected to the French parliament in 2009 and served as sports minister from September 2011 to May 2012. nigeria.title: Nasarawa vows peaceful polls, warns against electoral violence
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to conducting free, fair, transparent and peaceful elections, warning individuals and groups planning to instigate violence that they will be arrested and prosecuted. The State Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr. Nawani Aboki, gave the assurance while addressing journalists, stakeholders, party supporters and government partners in Lafia on Monday. Aboki said the government was monitoring the security situation across the state’s local government areas to ensure that voters could exercise their franchise without fear or intimidation. Warning those contemplating violence, the commissioner said the government’s preference for peace should not be mistaken for weakness. “Quietness does not mean that somebody is weak. At times, when someone is pushed, the time comes when they must act. “Anyone who wants to perpetuate violence will be arrested and prosecuted to ensure we have peaceful elections,” he warned. He urged political parties and candidates to conduct their campaigns in an orderly and civilised manner, stressing that political violence would serve no useful purpose in the electoral process or the development of the state. On voter participation, Aboki urged eligible residents to ensure their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) were ready and safely kept ahead of the elections. He advised voters against waiting until election day to collect their PVCs and encouraged those yet to register to take advantage of the online voter registration platform. Highlighting infrastructure and social development projects undertaken by the Federal Government and the administration of Governor Abdullahi Sule, the commissioner cited the proposed transformation of the Federal Polytechnic, Nasarawa, into a specialised mining university, as well as the Leather Designing and Craft School in Doma. On infrastructure, he listed the ongoing federal government dualisation and expansion of the Nasarawa-Keffi road network and the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Gombe Superhighway among projects expected to improve connectivity. In the health sector, Aboki said the upgrading and expansion of the Dalhatu Araf Specialist Hospital into the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, alongside facilities such as the Federal Eye Centre in Doma, had improved access to healthcare. The commissioner called on residents to support the All Progressives Congress (APC) gubernatorial candidate and other party candidates, arguing that such support would sustain the development initiatives of the Sule administration. “I know all of us are happy with the work Governor Sule has done. And so he has given us somebody we need to support. I want to call on all of us, and indeed the people of Nasarawa State, to support the candidate he has given us,” he said. nigeria.title: 2027: Support group targets 3.7m votes for Tinubu, Shettima
nigeria.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO – A grassroots mobilisation organisation, Global Survival for Grassroots Development and Empowerment Initiative (GSGDI), has announced plans to mobilise 3.7 million votes for President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima in the 2027 general elections. The target was announced following the organisation’s National Executive Council conference meeting in Abuja, where its leadership mapped out strategies to mobilise 100,000 votes in each of Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The National President of GSGDI, Ahmeed Olalekan Eshinlokun, said achieving the target would require discipline, sacrifice and collective responsibility among the organisation’s executives, members and grassroots coordinators. He urged members across the country to obtain valid Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and remain actively prepared to participate in the electoral process. Eshinlokun said the organisation’s nationwide mobilisation campaign would focus on political education, community engagement and responsible democratic participation. He added that GSGDI planned to deploy its nationwide network to ensure that five representatives were assigned to every polling unit as part of its grassroots mobilisation strategy. nigeria.title: Yobe enjoys relative peace across 17 LGAs – Buni
nigeria.description: …Says farmers now have access to farmlands By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has said the state now enjoys relative peace across its 17 local government areas following years of insurgency, with farmers and business operators able to pursue their activities without major security disruptions. Buni spoke on Sunday night in Abuja at the Yobe Development and Partnership Roundtable, where he engaged distinguished indigenes of the state residing outside the state. He said the improved security situation had enabled farmers to return to their farmlands, while business owners could move freely across communities to conduct legitimate commercial activities. “Yobe State today enjoys relative peace across the 17 local government areas. Our farmers in the last few years have had access to their farmlands, while businessmen and women continue to traverse the length and breadth of the state conducting legitimate businesses peacefully,” the governor said. Recalling the difficult period of insurgency, Buni said the state had suffered widespread killings, displacement, destruction of communities and loss of livelihoods. “A few years back, our story was different, pathetic and despicable. Yobe, our dear state, the Pride of the Sahel, was plagued by a reckless, brutal and senseless insurgency security challenge. Many people were killed, others maimed, several communities displaced, and the surviving victims lost their means of livelihood,” he said. He, however, commended the resilience of the people, saying their determination to overcome the challenges had contributed to the state’s recovery. Buni acknowledged that rebuilding the state was difficult, considering the limited resources available to the government and the extensive destruction caused by insecurity. He said his administration supported economic recovery by distributing farm machinery and other agricultural inputs to farmers free of charge to improve productivity, strengthen food security and promote economic growth. According to him, the government also maintained minimal tax charges for businesses and other commercial activities to enable operators to recover from the effects of the insurgency. He said the administration deliberately refrained from reviewing existing tax rates, which he described as outdated and unrealistic. On education, Buni said his administration declared a state of emergency in the sector, particularly at the primary and basic levels, upon assuming office. He listed the achievements under the programme to include the reconstruction of 301 schools, construction of 929 new classrooms and rehabilitation of 748 others. The governor added that the government established 15 mega and model schools, as well as 10 new Government Girls Senior Secondary Schools, to promote girl-child education. nigeria.title: Beyond the Asphalt: How Jetour’s High-Octane Lagos Convoy Brought Clean Water and Hope to Iwerekun Orile.
nigeria.description: On Saturday, September 19, 2026, the roar of modern horsepower met the rhythm of drumming and celebration in Iwerekun Orile, Ibeju Lekki. Jetour Nigeria proved that the ultimate destination of any journey isn’t just where the road ends, it’s the lives transformed along the way. As part of the “2026 Jetour Africa Expedition: A Road Trip Beyond Limits,” a striking fleet featuring the Jetour Dashing, X50, X70 Plus, X90 Plus, T2, T2 PHEV, X70 PHEV, and the flagship G700, embarked on an ambitious test of endurance. Following a vital road safety briefing by the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) Deputy Corps Commander Zonal Training Officer, Lagos, Mrs Esther Uzoma, and with seamless escort from the Nigeria Police Force and LASTMA, the convoy rolled out of Falomo Square, Ikoyi, turning heads across Victoria Island before pushing past the city’s glossy borders. Drivers and enthusiasts left the comfort of tarmac behind, putting the SUVs to the ultimate test across the unforgiving, swampy, and rock-strewn trails of the Coastal Highway. Yet, the real test of the day wasn’t mechanical resilience; it was human connection. The convoy’s final stop was the Roman Catholic Mission Primary School in Iwerekun Orile, where dust and exhaustion gave way to unbridled joy. There, Jetour officially commissioned a brand new, solar-powered borehole, delivering clean, reliable running water to a community that has spent generations yearning for it. The reception was deeply moving. School children broke into vibrant cultural dances, welcoming the convoy alongside elders, farmers, and market women. Beyond water, the team distributed food supplies to households, while pupils beamed with arms full of new books and refreshments. “This is where adventure meets purpose,” said Jetour Nigeria representative Kemi Adeola. “Our mission doesn’t stop at building capable vehicles; it lives in our pledge to drive tangible progress and touch the hearts of the communities we reach.” For the community, the impact was profound. High Chief Michael Oluwa hailed the water project as an unprecedented miracle in Iwerekun Orile’s history, pledging that the community would cherish and protect it. Equally overcome with emotion was the school’s head teacher, Mrs. Ariyike Bakre. “This is a special lifetime gift,” Bakre said, moved by the sight of water flowing on the school grounds. “It’s my first time seeing a solar-powered borehole. I am grateful to God for making this possible in my time, and for allowing our elders to witness this day. We cannot thank Jetour Nigeria enough, this water changes everything for our children and our people.” The day wound down at a tranquil beach lounge, where drivers and organizers gathered to celebrate the journey over good food, music, and shared memories. It was a fitting close to an unforgettable expedition: one that conquered demanding terrain, ignited the spirit of adventure, and left behind a lasting lifeline of clean water. nigeria.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
nigeria.description: The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday with an early fight over money as the UN’s chief urged world leaders to “get serious” about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes. Antonio Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN’s annual two-week climate conference. The summit comes after a year of punishing heatwaves in Europe, major wildfires in Indonesia and catastrophic floods in Nepal, with an exceptionally strong El Nino weather phenomenon fuelling more climate chaos. “We have entered a new age of climate extremes,” Guterres said in a statement. The UN secretary-general urged leaders to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”. The COP31 opening ceremony opened an hour-and-a-half late without explanation. Negotiators had been locked in discussions late Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda. “This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation. Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy. But poorer countries say the sums remain insufficient. Inventor said developed countries took a “hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations. A source familiar with the talks said the “climate finance work programme” would be included in the agenda. African countries had also pushed for the agenda to include the tripling of adaptation finance, which aims to help poorer nations pay for measures such as building sea walls or planting drought-resistant crops. The source said there would be no separate agenda point on tripling of adaptation finance but that it would be discussed under other items. A senior European Union official warned last week that there would be “no political will” for extra funding pledges at COP31. Observers say few major breakthroughs are expected at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The long-term climate outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. – Fossil fuel fight – Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference but raised concerns over how it would work. nigeria.title: World Entering ‘Age Of Climate Extremes,’ UN Chief Warns
nigeria.description: The world is entering a new reality where climate extremes are the norm, the United Nations chief Antonio Guterres warned Monday, urging leaders at the COP31 climate conference in Turkey to “get serious”. “A supersized El Niño is colliding with a planet already superheated by manmade climate change,” the UN secretary-general said in a statement. “We have entered a new age of climate extremes.” As leaders gathered in Antalya for the UN climate summit, Guterres called on them to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres speaks during the 15th ASEAN – United Nations (UN) Summit at the 47th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Kuala Lumpur on October 27, 2025. (Photo by Chalinee Thirasupa / POOL / AFP) | Chalinee Thirasupa / POOL / AFP His statement came as the UN’s World Meteorological Organisation released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels. Each of the past 12 years has been among the hottest 12 years on record, the agency said, with this year expected to be among the hottest ever. ‘Off The Charts’ “What we are seeing gives new meaning to the phrase off the charts,” WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva, cautioning that the current exceptionally strong El Niño could unleash more heat and extreme weather well into next year. “We should prepare for another record-breaking year in 2027.” The global average surface temperature between January and September this year was around 1.47 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial average, the WMO said. And this year’s El Niño — expected to be the strongest since 1950 at least — could push the figure higher by the end of the year. Preliminary data show 2026 ranking among the four hottest years on record, WMO climate information chief John Kenned told reporters, adding though that “with the El Niño developing, we might see when the final numbers come in that we’re close to the top”. The naturally occurring weather phenomenon releases heat from the ocean, which this year has been the warmest ever measured, Saulo pointed out. El Niño is declared when the sea surface temperature is half a degree above average in the tropical Pacific, but from now through January, WMO forecasts “it may be 3.8C above average”, she said. The WMO also reported that the global sea level was the highest on record, freshwater was dwindling and glaciers were continuing a long-term retreat. In 2025, the annual mass loss of ice was enough to fill five Olympic pools every second that year, it said. nigeria.title: Government offices shut in Osun as NLC directs workers strike
nigeria.description: Government offices in Osun were shut on Monday as workers embark on a three-day strike as directed by the state chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on Sunday. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the gates to the Osun Government Secretariat and the State House of Assembly in Osogbo were under lock with no workers or business activities ongoing in the premises. Similarly, the Olorunda Local Government Secretariat and Osogbo Local Government Secretariat gates were also locked. Students of public schools in Osogbo were also asked to return home, as teachers in public schools equally joined the strike. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that NLC Chairman in Osun, Christopher Arapasopo, and Secretary, Victor Amusan, in a statement on Sunday, directed all affiliate members of the congress to embark on a three-day sympathy strike with the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE). The NLC leadership explained that the strike followed the expiration of the seven-day ultimatum issued to the Federal and Osun governments over the continued withholding of the state local government statutory allocations. The NLC said that the issues raised concerning the local government allocations had remained unresolved. It said that after exhausting all reasonable avenues and in accordance with the resolutions reached at the emergency meeting of the State Executive Council (SEC) held on Oct. 28, all affiliate members of NLC were directed to embark on strike. nigeria.title: African players in Europe: Jackson scores as Villa squander leads at United
nigeria.description: Senegal star Nicolas Jackson scored after just four minutes for Aston Villa, who twice surrendered two-goal leads in a remarkable 4-4 Premier League draw away to Manchester United at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) Jackson put his side 2-0 ahead against United, but it wasn’t enough to inspire a victory at Old Trafford. When Jackson tapped in after United goalkeeper Senne Lammens palmed the ball into his path, it appeared the 25-year-old’s ninth goal in 14 games in all competitions this term would be the spark for a comfortable Villa win. But in an incredible finale, United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue a draw. YANN GBOHO (Coventry City) The Ivory Coast winger scored his first Premier League goal in a 3-1 defeat at Everton. Gboho, signed from French side Toulouse in September, put Coventry ahead with a composed finish after evading slack defending in the 52nd minute. But Frank Lampard’s team crumbled after the 25-year-old’s strike as Everton scored three times to leave the visitors one point above the relegation zone. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri continued his superb season with another goal to help Santander win 2-1 at Malaga. The 21-year-old bagged his ninth of the campaign with a simple finish to tuck a rebound home into the empty net. Only Raphinha, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal have scored more goals this season in La Liga. ITALY KONAN N’DRI (Lecce) After Angolan Kailonda Gaspar conceded a 60th-minute own goal to give Torino the lead in a clash of bottom-half Serie A clubs, Niger international N’Dri scored to salvage a 1-1 draw for visiting Lecce. The architect of the equaliser was Mali international Lassana Coulibaly. GERMANY EZECHIEL BANZUZI (RB Leipzig) Banzuzi’s goal proved the turning point as he kick-started Leipzig’s recovery to beat Augsburg 5-2 at home in the Bundesliga after conceding inside the opening minute. Anton Kade had Augsburg in front after 36 seconds but Banzuzi levelled in the 33rd minute when he turned a Brajan Gruda pass into the bottom right corner. The 21-year-old Democratic Republic of Congo internnational has two goals and two assists in the league this season. With Leipzig 5-1 up, Augsburg’s Alexis Claude Maurice intercepted the ball and sent his side in the other direction. Fabian Rieder latched on to Claude Maurice’s pass before finding Ogundu, who slid the ball into the bottom corner. FRANCE LASSINE SINAYOKO (Paris FC) Ligue 1’s leading scorer Sinayoko netted after 63 minutes to give third-placed Paris FC a 1-0 win at lowly Auxerre. nigeria.title: Trump says Iran war ‘highly unlikely’ to resume
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely,” ahead of a meeting with mediator Qatar’s prime minister on Monday. Trump has threatened to resume strikes in recent weeks, with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could restart after last Tuesday’s midterm elections. The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.” “I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said. Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is also the country’s foreign minister, at the White House on Monday. The meeting will be Trump’s first with a foreign leader since a massive midterm loss that saw his Republican Party lose control of Congress. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested on Sunday that peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the vote was being assessed. “For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television. “We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward,” he added. – ‘They had enough’ – Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran — which began with US-Israeli strikes in late February — was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat. Araghchi said Monday that the US president “clearly recognizes that the vast majority of Americans are disgusted with Israel.” “Americans are evidently sick and tired of Israel bamboozling US administrations into Forever Wars,” Araghchi said on X. “They had enough. So has our region.” In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms. “They’re a failing nation. entertainment.title: How Seyi Ademeso Turned Awkwardness Into the Meshkiey Brand
entertainment.description: Some people spend years trying to avoid awkward situations. Seyi Ademeso has built a career out of creating them, in the identity of Meshkiey . The content creator has turned everyday social discomfort into a distinctive style of comedy, earning an audience that recognises him for his unconventional approach to skits. But there is more to Seyi than the character who seems willing to embarrass himself for a laugh. Beyond the camera, he is a creative strategist, entrepreneur and businessman with ambitions that stretch far beyond social media. In this exclusive, we sat down with him to talk about the journey, the person behind the persona and what he hopes to build next. Hello Meshkiey. How are you feeling today? I’m feeling good. Honestly, I’m grateful. I’m excited to have this conversation and reflect on the journey. Before Meshkiey became the person people know online, what were you like growing up? I think I’ve always been a very observant person. Even growing up, I noticed little things about people, the way they behaved, the way they spoke, the funny things people did without realising they were funny. I was also quite expressive. I wouldn’t necessarily say I was the loudest person in every room, but I definitely had a personality. I liked making people laugh, and I enjoyed doing things differently. Looking back, I think a lot of the things people now associate with Meshkiey were actually already there. The difference is that I eventually found a platform where I could turn those traits into something creative. When did you start creating, really? I started creating around 2016, and honestly, there wasn’t some grand master plan behind it. I think I just wanted to create. I had a phone, I had ideas, and I was fascinated by what people were doing online. At the time, content creation wasn’t necessarily viewed as a serious career path the way it is today. My early content was very different from what people know me for now. I was experimenting a lot, trying different formats and figuring out what felt natural to me. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. sports.description: Back in his native Southern California, C.J. Stroud turned in one of the best games of his career as the Texans stayed in the playoff hunt with a win over the Chargers. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) INGLEWOOD, Calif. - When C.J. Stroud woke up in his hotel bed Sunday morning in downtown Los Angeles, he was still feeling under the weather. All week he had been dealing with some kind of illness that he said gave him chills and "all the things." He said he barely practiced Thursday. Whatever he had, it was still with him. Yet, some six hours later, he went on to have one of the best games of his career. Stroud, who was playing in front of friends and family near his hometown of Rancho Cucamonga , threw for a season-high 384 yards, a career-high five touchdowns and just one interception in Houston's 44-22 rout of the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) on Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium. The 44 points scored were a season high for the Texans' offense, which has often delivered time and time again, especially on the road. The Texans improved to 3-5 on the season. It was the type of performance that will put Stroud in the MVP conversation if he can continue playing this way. It is the type of performance that will have some suggesting that the Texans can make a run towards the playoffs. "He really gives that confidence to the entire team," coach DeMeco Ryans said of Stroud. "When the defensive guys, they see him up making plays, everyone is excited. Everyone knows the type of energy, the type of momentum that that brings to our entire team when he's making those plays and he's done it all year." The Texans are currently 1 ½ games behind the Patriots for that final wild-card spot with nine games remaining. They face the Browns, who are also 1 ½ games ahead of them, next Sunday in Cleveland. But based on their upcoming schedule, and how Stroud is playing, anything is possible, especially if the defense can gain some momentum too. Though the performance from the defense wasn't perfect, Sunday's game against the NFL's worst offense was a step in the right direction. The Texans tied a franchise record with eight sacks on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. They also forced two turnovers - an interception by cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. and a fumble. But the offense, which had 485 yards of total offense, was the story of this game. And it started with Stroud, who became just the fourth quarterback younger than 26 years old with at least 350 passing yards and five touchdown passes in multiple games, joining Patrick Mahomes, Dan Marino and Matthew Stafford. The other game Stroud achieved that stat line was during his 2023 rookie season, when he threw five touchdowns in a thrilling 39-37 win over the Bucs . The Frenchman suffered an inadvertent elbow to his face. He still scored two free throws with blood coming out of his nose, but he didn’t return after being diagnosed with a fracture. sports.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes pushed through a serious hit in their 35-12 win over the New York Jets. Mahomes did not miss a single offensive snap in the win, going 23/31 on pass attempts for 242 yards, two TDs, and a 117.9 passer rating. He also rushed for eight yards on two carries in a strong performance. Mahomes was tackled by Jets EDGE David Bailey in the second quarter and appeared to suffer an elbow injury, but his resolute toughness made him push through the discomfort and finish the win after avoiding major injury. Patrick Mahomes hailed as a cyborg by Nick Wright Watching Mahomes take that rough hit and escape without injury left FOX Sports’ Nick Wright in awe of the 33-year-old QB. “Also… Never a doubt. Mahomes is a cyborg. 99% of QBs have their elbow dislocated on that hit. He missed zero snaps. They’ll be 8-2 heading into Buffalo.” It’s since been confirmed that Mahomes’ injury is an elbow strain/sprain after post-game MRIs, with the QB likely not missing their game against the Atlanta Falcons on November 15. Mahomes admitted after the win that the hit from Bailey had a major impact on his performance, as he struggled to throw the ball as deep and precisely as he normally can. Nonetheless, even a slightly wounded Mahomes would be a better option than backup QB Justin Fields for the Chiefs right now, especially as they look to challenge the 7-2 Denver Broncos for THE top spot in the AFC West. While Mahomes has not been among the MVP contenders this season, he has had a strong comeback season after rushing through recovery from a torn ACL. Over the season, Mahomes has thrown 177/263 for 2,037 yards, 14 TDs, and four INTs for a 101.8 passer rating. Avoiding a season-ending elbow injury on that play was a moment of good fortune for the Chiefs, and the franchise will hope that fortune pushes them through till the end of the season. sports.title: Three-time Olympic judo champion announces bid for French presidency
sports.description: Three-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner is to run for the French presidency, with his campaign intending to “show that we can turn France around”. The 37-year-old said he would not run on a left- or right-wing ticket but instead focus his campaign on “bringing the French people together”, with the slogan for his campaign “The France we want”. He told French outlet Le Parisien on Monday: “France is a great country. It has allowed me to become the person I am today and has given me the opportunity to dream big. “Today, that’s what’s missing. That ambition is gone; that hope is gone. “I see a divide in society across the country, but I do not accept what I hear in the mouths of young people, that it is difficult today to imagine a future. That is why I decided to commit myself, alongside the French people, and to become a candidate for the presidency.” Riner has no experience of politics but is a well-known and popular figure in France, and has previously hinted at a desire to enter politics at the highest level. He said in an interview last year: “I am a citizen above all, not just a sportsperson. If tomorrow I enter politics, it wouldn’t be to be a minister, it would be to change things. The best role would be president.” Riner, who was born in Guadeloupe, grew up in Paris. He is a nine-time heavyweight world champion, two-time openweight world champion, and has two Olympic bronze medals to go with his three individual golds and two mixed team gold medals. He was a torchbearer during the Olympic torch relay ahead of the 2024 Games in Paris, and lit the cauldron during the opening ceremony alongside retired sprinter Marie-Jose Perec. Riner said that the experience of the home Olympic Games uniting the country inspired him to enter politics, saying: “I saw a whole country come together, proud, happy. I thought to myself, what we have been able to do for 15 days, we must be able to do for the country.” He said his decision to run for president would not end his judo career or hopes of competing at the LA Games 2028.

technology.title: AI echo chambers and sanity in tech leadership: Three case studies
technology.description: "AI delusion" remains loosely defined, but most of us know it when we see it: exaggerated faith in the technology's power, applicability, or nature, coupled with a refusal to acknowledge its limitations. It's bad in the individual, as when an elderly relative emails you a hallucination-laden ChatGPT summary. It's worse in management, when your boss insists that AI slop is genius marketing content at a bargain rate. It is terrifying in tech CEOs. It is not, thankfully, compulsory. Consider three recent examples of technology leadership in the age of AI. One would be Pythonesque were the disconnect with engineers and the public not so profound. Another risks becoming a business-school case study in how to demolish customer trust. The third offers something less fashionable: robust pragmatism. Saving the best till last, y'all. Case 1: we present for your consideration Sam Altman of OpenAI, one of the few actually at the controls of the singularity machine. It seems churlish to pluck just one luscious fruit out of that cornucopia of choices, yet we must. Sam Altman thinks it is a sin against the natural order that so much RAM is idling in machines owned by individuals, organizations, and anywhere that isn't Big AI . It's oh so inefficient. How convenient that the efficient allocation of scarce resources should favor the business he runs. Free market schmarket. Altman has since said his remarks were taken out of context and that he wants consumers to have as much memory as they like. The efficiency argument still reveals whose priorities come first. This is the best kind of delusion, one with an undeniable truth at its core – memory does indeed get used far more intensively in AI model makers and inference servers than in your laptop. For a business selling the future, treating privately owned hardware as an inefficient allocation of resources has a distinctly Soviet flavor, and the American right has vowed to stamp out socialist extremism. Get on with it, chaps, you've only got two years left . That Altman can't see this is the best bit of the misconception. There are two potential root causes of this Marxist-Leninist-Altmanism. One is that he's mathed the math and worked out that the only way OpenAI can hit the numbers is if it gets every last byte in the world, hot off the fab. The other is that you can't run on-prem on an 8 GB state-mandated Chromebook, and on-prem is otherwise going to twist his melon until it falls off. technology.title: Portal breach at Germany's top university exposes every registered user's password
technology.description: Attackers stole central university login passwords belonging to everyone registered with the Technical University of Munich's myTUM portal, including an admin whose credentials were then used to attack a second system. TUM restored access to its TUMonline campus management system on Monday morning, allowing users to change their passwords. The university disclosed the attack on November 6. The initial attack targeted the myTUM portal, which serves students and faculty members, providing centralized online access to services and documents. TUM said the attackers used the admin's credentials to launch a follow-on attack on TUMonline, its central campus management system, which forced the IT team to take it offline. The university has not disclosed how the attackers initially gained access or how the stolen passwords were stored. It did not immediately answer questions about the number of affected users. It also did not specify whether this sysadmin had multi-factor authentication (MFA) switched on, but it confirmed that "user accounts with MFA were protected from this attack." Attackers may also have accessed names, home addresses, and dates of birth. Potentially exposed employee records included work addresses and phone numbers, while student records included ID numbers, degree programs, and completed semesters. "The attackers' access within TUMonline was largely logged," said Dr Alexander Braun, CIO at TUM, in the disclosure. "After analyzing these logs, we currently assume that no other data from TUMonline was compromised, such as grades or college applications. We are continuing to investigate this." TUM is directing users to reset their passwords through Microsoft 365 where possible. Those without MFA already configured must instead use a German electronic ID or request a reset email while connected to the campus network. The university also warned users to watch for phishing and fraud, and to change any passwords reused elsewhere. TUM ranks first in Germany and 25th worldwide in the QS university rankings. The STEM-focused institution reports 51,954 students across its German campuses and TUM Asia in Singapore, plus 12,850 employees. ®

technology.title: Torrent underground
technology.description: When Jane first heard about Memory and Imagination , a rare 1990s documentary about the Library of Congress, she was intrigued. But the Canadian writer in her 30s couldn’t find the movie anywhere — not on streaming services, not on YouTube, not on pirate sites — and her intrigue turned into obsession. Worried it might become a lost film , Jane decided to scour auction sites, search every library catalog she could think of, and even enlist some of her online acquaintances to find a copy. Her plan was to “share it with other people to help ensure it would be preserved into the future,” as she puts it. Jane knew the perfect tool for the task: a private torrent tracker. “I am ethically conflicted about piracy. I often feel guilty about it.” Private trackers are essentially the speakeasies of the online piracy world. Promoted primarily by word of mouth, they rely on secrecy, exclusivity, and strict community rules to shield everything that’s going on behind closed doors from the public’s prying eyes. What unites these communities is that they all use BitTorrent to trade media among like-minded file sharers. But their focuses range widely, from general-purpose trackers with catalogs so broad that they make Netflix look like a niche service to the many specialized communities for categories like Chinese movies, motorsports, visual effects tools, e-learning courses, and Japanese porn. There’s even a private tracker just for Frank Zappa music. Private trackers are known for massive and meticulously organized catalogs, which they owe to users like Jane, who, like every other pirate I talked to for this story, opted to be identified by a pseudonym due to the terabytes of copyrighted data they’ve been sharing. These are people willing to go the extra mile to find long-forgotten movies, rare concert recordings, or out-of-print books. “Many private tracker users are fully consumed with archive fever,” she says. At first, Jane had no luck finding a physical copy of that elusive documentary, which includes interviews with Steve Jobs and Julia Child. Nobody was selling it on eBay. Her local public library didn’t have it. Neither did any other public library in North America. And when she finally located a DVD that was available to the public, it was in the Bibliotheca Alexandrina — Egypt’s modern-day re-creation of the ancient library that’s long been synonymous with lost media. “That bowled me over,” Jane says. “This obscure movie I’m looking for is only available in the Library of Alexandria!” Eventually, Jane found Memory and Imagination for sale on a small online marketplace for historical media. Jane instantly bought a copy and uploaded it. “It looked like a digital rip of a severely degraded VHS tape,” she says. “I was still over the moon [that] I rescued this historically significant documentary.” Not everyone who uses private trackers shares Jane’s amateur-archivist zeal. technology.title: AI Slop FM radio experiment puts machines on trial, one dodgy tune at a time
technology.description: A Welsh music enthusiast has built an internet radio station that plays AI-generated tunes alongside human-made tracks without telling listeners which is which, to find out whether listeners really hate AI music or just the idea of it. AI Slop FM is the creation of Mike Chaffin, who built and runs the station single-handedly from Ammanford, Carmarthenshire. By stripping away artist names, cover art, and any mention of AI, Chaffin hopes to find out what listeners really think when they have nothing but the music to go on. The free 24/7 station asks listeners to rate tracks from S to E, tag how the music makes them feel, and leave written feedback. The most popular submissions will eventually make it into a weekly chart called the Slop 40, giving creators something that can be hard to come by in the age of streaming: an actual audience. Anyone can submit a track, including human musicians, although Chaffin has already discovered that not all of them are particularly keen on the idea. He told The Register that he had floated the idea to an unsigned musician friend who had sold around 600 albums, but was met with a rather nervous response. "Wh, wh, why would I want to do that?" the musician reportedly asked, according to Chaffin, who said he had never heard his friend stutter before. "It seems that there is a deep rooted fear of AI music in the industry," Chaffin said. The station is still in beta, with Chaffin waiting for enough submissions to fill its schedule across different genres before opening it fully. He's already been pleasantly surprised by the quality of the music submitted, although he still listens to every track to make sure nobody is trying to pass off Bohemian Rhapsody as their own work. Among the early offerings are what Chaffin describes as a developing genre of slightly rude protest songs about HR departments, along with an operatic epic about a blocked toilet. "Some of which are hilarious," he said of the HR songs. As for the toilet opera, it "runs through my head about once a day, whether I like it or not." Chaffin believes the sheer volume of music uploaded to streaming platforms means plenty of perfectly decent tracks never find an audience, whether a person or a machine made them. He hopes AI Slop FM will give some of those overlooked creations a chance to be heard. "You don't have to have published your creations to upload. Just to own the rights," he explained. Tracks that don't make the Slop 40 could still get another outing, with plans for genre-specific stations offering unsuccessful submissions a second chance. The bigger question is what happens when listeners start rating AI-generated music more highly than the human competition, but Chaffin isn't particularly worried about that. technology.title: Memory crunch makes refurbished kit look a lot less secondhand
technology.description: Rising memory prices are pushing more customers toward refurbished tech, suppliers say, with warranties of up to three years helping to make secondhand kit a less daunting purchase. Memory costs have more than quadrupled this year as manufacturers prioritize more lucrative high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for servers powering AI datacenters. Many enterprises are keeping equipment longer in an uncertain economy. Ben Caddy, senior analyst at Omdia, said suppliers were linking refresh discussions with opportunities to recover value from customers' aging kit. By 2030, he predicted, 35 percent of "all the hardware sold for the channel will be taken back by partners," driven "by the sheer economic logic of taking equipment back, recovering value, and embracing more circular IT lifecycles." This is already helping some customers "unlock some capital to put towards those [relatively] small refresh plans," he said while hosting a panel on circular IT at last month's Canalys Forums in Barcelona. Refurbished smartphones are growing in popularity, but persuading customers to trade in their old devices remains a constraint on supply. The same applies to PCs and other equipment, said Jon Sansom, MD at GreenSafe IT. "Availability is a challenge," he said. Marcel Joosten, group director of marketing and digital commerce at tech lifecycle specialist XTENTEC, said the company now offers trade-ins when customers buy new kit. "We're actually financing the residual value" at the end of year two, three, or four, when customers return the equipment, he told the audience. XTENTEC collects, refurbishes, rents, and resells equipment, and has an agreement with HP to renovate aging products, with a two or even three-year warranty available as "just an SKU on the list from HP." Joosten said equivalent support, including HP Care Pack services, helped make refurbished equipment more attractive to buyers. Customers want to cut their carbon footprint, and many public and private sector tenders require it. But the "most important thing" for many is trust, said Patrick Molberg, CEO of Advania Finance. "The customers have to trust the refurbished equipment and have to trust the process. And I think one of the things that we have to be better at as a whole is that we kind of need to have a standard methodology regarding verification." Work on verification standards with vendors including HP, Lenovo, and Dell is ongoing, Molberg said. He also argued that lifecycle services should be built into purchasing decisions rather than added three or four years later. Joosten argued that listed US tech companies' focus on quarterly sales and market share can work against refurbishment. "That needs to change," he said. "I think there should be a market share figure for circularity." ®

technology.description: Welcome to Monday, the day upon which The Register offers a new instalment of " Who, Me? " – our reader-contributed column that shares your stories of messing up, 'fessing up, and somehow finding redress. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Oriel" who told us he once worked for a vendor of small business accounting software. This story comes from a time when software shipped on CD-ROMs and users bought it off the shelf in actual shops. The vendor released a new version each year and always shipped it before a major holiday that's celebrated with a giant meal. Oriel was part of the team whose job it was to get the package ready on time. In the previous year, they flubbed the job because the program didn't always install itself on some PCs running Windows 95 or Windows ME machines system due to registry corruption. "We wanted to increase our successful installation metrics, so in conjunction with the installation team, a key decision was made – by me – to force the updating of registry keys to enable the install," Oriel admitted. In his email to The Register , he asked the portentous question: "What could possibly go wrong?" What went wrong was that not long after the software was shipped, the vendor's support lines started getting calls from customers who complained that after installing the accounting package none of their other software would work. "Installing a new version of our application had borked the customer's machine completely," Oriel wrote. The company decided the best thing to do was to tell affected customers they should go and buy a new PC – and that it would pick up the bill, no questions asked. "In the week prior to the holiday, we replaced over 600 machines," Oriel told The Register . "To get a reproduction case we need a user's machine where the user had created a Windows Registry restore point prior to installing our application," Oriel explained.
